goal: Contain and report payload-time source failures per file across every transfer route without corrupting adjacent records, committing invalid data, or aborting the remaining transfer.
recommended_approach: Keep contract v7, exact-length shard preparation, chunk-framed records, terminal statuses, and the unified need ledger, but use stable manifest-entry IDs; handle lossy names during manifest processing; define complete resume transitions including zero-block completion; read and validate through the same opened source handle on every route; and use a containment-preserving sink transaction that stages full-file replacements, drains rejected records, and commits only after a successful terminator.
comparison: The reviewed plan has the right overall architecture and strong acceptance coverage, so replacement is unnecessary, but it is not yet the best approach: its in-place full-file abort behavior can destroy a good backup, its resume state machine rejects valid terminal-only records, its proposed sink API omits existing destination-open containment, its local fast paths can validate a different file than they copy, and its lossy path identity can suppress or misattribute failures.
material_changes: Stage full-file destination writes and atomically replace the target only after successful record completion; retain the separately ruled in-place behavior for resume patches.

Make a stable manifest-entry ID the protocol and ledger identity, detect destination-path collisions, and process name_lossy entries as failures during manifest/diff handling even when no payload is requested.
Add resume ledger transitions for the first block and for successful or failed BlockComplete arriving directly from Granted when no block was emitted.
Redesign begin_record so containable destination-open failures return a draining/discarding record state rather than a session-fatal error, and derive the final ledger state from the sink outcome.
Require local copying and post-copy validation to use the same opened source object; path-reopening fast paths must be replaced or given an identity-safe descriptor-based implementation.

findings.title: A failed full-file replacement destroys the last good destination copy
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:55 — the plan generalizes the resume decision into no staged writes and specifies removing the destination on abort; docs/DECISIONS.md:150 limits the cited ruling to an in-place resume patch.
findings.predicted_failure: If the source fails after an existing destination file has been truncated, the run reports a contained skip but leaves the backup path absent, destroying the last known-good copy before a successful rerun.
findings.better_approach: Stage full-file records beside the target and atomically replace on successful commit; abort removes only the staging file, while resume block updates can remain in-place under the existing ruling.

findings.title: Terminal-only resume records have no legal state transition
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:243 — BlockComplete is accepted only from Active(Resume), but no transition makes a resume grant Active before a block; crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/data_plane.rs:2239 — the current protocol validly claims BlockComplete directly from the live grant, including when zero blocks were emitted.
findings.predicted_failure: A resume whose blocks already match, or whose source fails before emitting its first differing block, sends BlockComplete while the ledger remains Granted and is rejected as a protocol violation, aborting the session.
findings.better_approach: Transition Granted(resume) to Active on the first block, and permit successful or failed BlockComplete directly from Granted as the zero-block terminal case, recording and validating its lane.

findings.title: The new sink lifecycle omits existing destination-open containment
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:305 — begin_record returns Result<Box<dyn RecordWriter>> and is described as opening the target, with no contained-rejection state; crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/sink.rs:1168 — the current sink drains the complete record and returns per_file_failure when destination creation fails containably.
findings.predicted_failure: A destination path that cannot be opened can make begin_record return an error and abort the whole session, regressing the already-shipped behavior that drains and reports only that file.
findings.better_approach: Have begin_record return either a real writer or a discard writer carrying the contained destination failure; both consume framing through the terminator, and only path-safety, volume, or transport failures return Err.

findings.title: Local validation can inspect a different file than the fast copy reads
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:413 — the plan opens and re-stats one handle while retaining whole-file zero-copy paths; crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/sink.rs:1398 — the current local cascade calls path-based copy_file(src, dst), which reopens the source independently.
findings.predicted_failure: If an application atomically replaces the source path after the validation handle opens, the fast copy can read the replacement while the post-copy check re-stats the old handle, allowing bytes or size from the wrong file to be finalized under the manifest header.
findings.better_approach: Pass the opened descriptor through the local copy cascade and implement buffered, copy_file_range, fcopyfile, or equivalent descriptor-based paths; disable path-only fast paths where identity cannot be preserved.

findings.title: Lossy names can evade reporting or collide before payload handling
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:482 — name_lossy is acted on only by source payload paths and the destination is said not to need it; crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/mod.rs:1922 — retained manifest headers are inserted into a HashMap keyed only by the lossy relative_path.
findings.predicted_failure: A lossy entry judged already converged never reaches a payload path and exits without the required failure, while an invalid-byte name colliding with a legitimate U+FFFD name overwrites one retained header and can cause the wrong file to be skipped or a protocol abort.
findings.better_approach: Assign each manifest entry an opaque ID used by needs, records, skips, terminators, and ledgers; at manifest intake, record name_lossy entries as failures regardless of diff outcome and explicitly reject or report duplicate destination paths.
